explain.say: The Guru Granth Sahib is the holy scripture of Sikhism, and Sikhs honour it not just as a book but as their living Guru. It is a collection of hymns, called Gurbani, the Guru's word, written to be sung in praise of the one Creator.

draw.text: Gurbani: the Guru's word, sung as hymns
It opens with Ik Onkar: there is one Creator

explain.say: The fifth Guru, Guru Arjan, gathered the hymns of the Gurus and other saints into the Adi Granth, and installed it in the Harmandir Sahib, the Golden Temple in Amritsar, in 1604.

draw.label: Amritsar, home of the Golden Temple, and Nankana Sahib, birthplace of Guru Nanak

draw.text: 1604: the Adi Granth installed in the Golden Temple

explain.say: In 1708, the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, declared that after him there would be no more human Gurus. The scripture itself would be the Guru forever, which is why it is called the Guru Granth Sahib.

items: 1469: Guru Nanak, the first Guru, is born
1604: Guru Arjan installs the Adi Granth
1708: Guru Gobind Singh names it the eternal Guru

draw.text: Ten human Gurus, then the Guru Granth Sahib

explain.say: Every standard copy has exactly 1,430 pages, called angs, written in the Gurmukhi script. Its hymns are arranged by raga, the musical mode in which each should be sung.

items: Opening | Mool Mantar and Japji Sahib

explain.say: It contains hymns by six Sikh Gurus, and also by saints from other backgrounds, Hindu and Muslim, such as Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev and Sheikh Farid. It teaches devotion to one God, equality of all people, honest work, sharing and service.

faq.q: Why is the Guru Granth Sahib called a Guru?
faq.a: Before he died in 1708, the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, declared that there would be no more human Gurus and that the scripture would be the eternal Guru. Sikhs therefore honour it as a living Guru, the guide for their lives.
asks: Why do Sikhs treat their holy book as a Guru?
What does eternal Guru mean?
Is the Guru Granth Sahib a person?

faq.q: Who compiled the Guru Granth Sahib?
faq.a: The fifth Guru, Guru Arjan, compiled the first version, the Adi Granth, in 1604, with the scribe Bhai Gurdas. Guru Gobind Singh later added the hymns of his father, the ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur.
asks: Who wrote the Guru Granth Sahib?
What is the Adi Granth?
When was the Guru Granth Sahib written?

faq.q: How many pages are in the Guru Granth Sahib?
faq.a: The standard Guru Granth Sahib has 1,430 pages, called angs, which means limbs, because Sikhs see it as the body of the Guru. Every copy uses the same layout, so a hymn is always on the same ang.
asks: What is an ang?
How long is the Guru Granth Sahib?
Why are the pages called angs?

faq.q: What language is the Guru Granth Sahib written in?
faq.a: It is written in the Gurmukhi script. Its hymns use Punjabi and several related languages of north India, with words from Sanskrit, Persian and others, so it could be understood across the region.
asks: What is Gurmukhi?
Is the Guru Granth Sahib in Punjabi?
What script is Sikh scripture in?

faq.q: Who wrote the hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib?
faq.a: It contains hymns by six of the Sikh Gurus, starting with Guru Nanak, and also by Hindu and Muslim saints, such as Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev and Sheikh Farid. Guru Arjan contributed the most hymns.
asks: Does the Guru Granth Sahib include other religions?
Which saints are in the Guru Granth Sahib?
Are there Muslim hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib?

faq.q: Why are the hymns arranged by raga?
faq.a: The hymns are meant to be sung, so they are grouped by raga, the musical mode that sets their mood, with 31 main ragas. Singing them, called kirtan, is a central part of Sikh worship.
asks: What is a raga in Sikh scripture?
What is kirtan?
Is the Guru Granth Sahib sung?

faq.a: The Mool Mantar is the opening statement of the Guru Granth Sahib, composed by Guru Nanak. It begins Ik Onkar, there is one Creator, and describes God as truth, without fear or hatred, beyond time and self existent.
asks: How does the Guru Granth Sahib begin?
What does Ik Onkar mean?
What is the first verse of the Guru Granth Sahib?

faq.a: Japji Sahib is a prayer by Guru Nanak that comes right after the Mool Mantar at the start of the Guru Granth Sahib. Many Sikhs recite it every morning.
asks: What is the morning prayer of Sikhs?
Who wrote Japji Sahib?
What is Japji?

faq.q: How is the Guru Granth Sahib treated in a gurdwara?
faq.a: It is placed on a raised throne under a canopy, covered with fine cloths, and an attendant waves a whisk called a chaur over it. Each night it is carried to a resting room in a ceremony called Sukhasan, and opened again in the morning.
asks: Why is the Guru Granth Sahib put to bed at night?
What is a chaur?
Where is the Guru Granth Sahib kept?

faq.a: A hukamnama is a passage read after the Guru Granth Sahib is opened at a random page, usually in the morning. Sikhs take it as the Guru's guidance for that day.
asks: What is the daily reading in a gurdwara?
What is a vak?
Why do Sikhs open the scripture at random?

faq.a: An Akhand Path is a continuous reading of the whole Guru Granth Sahib, from beginning to end without a break, by a team of readers. It takes about 48 hours and is held for special occasions.
asks: How long does it take to read the Guru Granth Sahib?
What is a continuous reading?
When do Sikhs read the whole scripture?

faq.q: What does the Guru Granth Sahib teach?
faq.a: It teaches devotion to the one Creator, remembering God's name, and that all people are equal whatever their caste, gender or religion. It also stresses honest work, sharing with others and selfless service.
asks: What are the main teachings of the Guru Granth Sahib?
What is the message of Sikh scripture?
What does Gurbani teach?

faq.q: Why do people cover their heads in a gurdwara?
faq.a: Covering the head and removing shoes are signs of respect in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib. Everyone, Sikh or not, is welcome, and is asked to do the same.
asks: Do I need to cover my head in a gurdwara?
Can non Sikhs visit a gurdwara?
Why take off shoes in a gurdwara?

facts: The standard Guru Granth Sahib has 1,430 pages, called angs, in the Gurmukhi script.
Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth and installed it in the Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar, in 1604.
In 1708 Guru Gobind Singh declared the scripture the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.
The Guru Granth Sahib includes hymns by six Sikh Gurus and by saints such as Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev and Sheikh Farid.
Its hymns are arranged in 31 main ragas, or musical modes.

quiz.say: Which Guru declared that the scripture would be the eternal Guru of the Sikhs?
quiz.show: Who made the scripture the eternal Guru?
quiz.why: In 1708 the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, ended the line of human Gurus and named the scripture the eternal Guru.

wrong.0: Guru Nanak was the first Guru and founder of Sikhism, long before the scripture was compiled.
wrong.1: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth in 1604, but did not declare it the Guru.

quiz.say: A visitor notices that the Guru Granth Sahib includes hymns by Kabir and Sheikh Farid, who were not Sikh Gurus. What does this show about the scripture?
quiz.show: Why include hymns by saints who were not Sikh Gurus?

options.show: It honours truth wherever it is found
options.say: It honours devotion and truth wherever they are found

options.show: The Gurus ran out of hymns
options.say: The Gurus ran out of hymns

options.show: It was a mistake by a scribe
options.say: It was a mistake by a scribe

quiz.why: The Gurus chose hymns that shared their message of devotion to one God and equality, whatever the writer's background.

wrong.1: The Gurus themselves wrote thousands of hymns; these were chosen on purpose.
wrong.2: The selection was made carefully by Guru Arjan, not by accident.

quiz.say: Every printed copy of the Guru Granth Sahib has the same 1,430 angs, with each hymn on the same page. Why is that useful?
quiz.show: Why does every copy have the same 1,430 angs?

options.show: A hymn can be found on the same ang anywhere
options.say: A hymn can be found on the same ang in any copy, anywhere

quiz.why: A fixed layout means Sikhs everywhere can refer to a hymn by its ang number and find exactly the same words.

wrong.1: The layout does not change the weight; it keeps every copy identical.
wrong.2: There are copies in gurdwaras all over the world.
